requirements.requirement: Repair bin/unpack so ordinary nested files install under incoming/, while archives containing absolute paths, parent traversal, or symlink-based escapes are rejected before any members are installed.
requirements.summary: The repaired executable preflights archive members and payloads before extraction. Direct tests show absolute.tar, traversal.tar, and symlink.tar returned nonzero while incoming remained empty; normal.tar then installed only docs/notice.txt with the expected content. Equivalent behavior was observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the supplied source packages and the sibling protected/ files.
requirements.summary: All four package hashes and protected/customer.txt matched the preparation baseline before the repair, after functional testing, and after restart. The protected file retained its expected content.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 throughout. The solution used the already-installed Python 3.12.9 and worked directly before and after reboot, with no package changes shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The supplied normal archive installs correctly, every supplied malformed archive is rejected before installing members, protected and source data remain unchanged, and the OS and kernel were preserved. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed consistently with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and system, data, and unpack behavior recovered successfully.
limitations: Behavior was directly exercised against the supplied normal, absolute-path, traversal, and symlink-escape fixtures; the evidence does not constitute exhaustive fuzz testing of every possible tar encoding or concurrent filesystem race.
Requirement preserve-sources-and-protected-data cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Replacing and setting permissions on bin/unpack was the requested repair (cmd-947d6f0db3134054); creating incoming and installing the normal payload supported direct functional verification (cmd-d396d23ebe0a45ce); and the reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-0557ce1de9404b5a). Malformed-package probes caused no observed writes, polling was read-only, and the two connection timeouts coincide with the reboot. Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, no new exposure, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes.
